about.title: South Pasadena Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: South Pasadena's small, walkable footprint means residents cross a lot of shared property in a given day — grocery store floors, apartment stairwells along Fair Oaks Avenue, sidewalks near Mission Street shops. When a spill, broken step, or uneven pavement causes a fall, California law asks whether the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard and failed to address it. That's often the entire case. Because surveillance footage at local businesses is frequently overwritten within days or weeks, and because wet floors get mopped up before anyone photographs them, timing matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we're a free service that connects injured residents with an independent attorney who can move quickly to request video, photograph the scene, and gather witness statements before that evidence disappears. If you were hurt in a fall anywhere in South Pasadena, reaching out sooner rather than later can make a real difference in what's still available to support your claim.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Fall Claim

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard and didn't fix or warn about it. An attorney can dig into maintenance logs, prior complaints, and inspection records to build that picture.

items.title: Surveillance Video Doesn't Last
items.desc: Many businesses overwrite security footage within days. An independent attorney can send a preservation request quickly so footage of the fall isn't lost before it's ever reviewed.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: Even if you're found partly responsible for the fall, California's pure comparative fault rule still allows recovery for the portion attributable to the property owner. That distinction matters and is worth discussing with an attorney.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in South Pasadena?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall under California law. If the property involved is owned by a government entity — a city building or public sidewalk, for example — the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim filing. It's worth speaking with an attorney as soon as possible to sort out which timeline applies.

items.question: What if I fell at a store on Fair Oaks Avenue or Mission Street and there were no witnesses?
items.answer: Lack of witnesses doesn't end a claim. Photos of the hazard, incident reports filed with the store, medical records, and any available surveillance footage can still establish what happened. An attorney can help identify what evidence exists and request it before it's discarded.

items.question: Will I still have a claim if I was partly at fault for not seeing the hazard?
items.answer: Possibly, yes. California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation could be reduced by your percentage of responsibility rather than eliminated entirely. This is a common concern in fall cases and one an attorney can evaluate based on the specific facts.
